title: A small update description does not guarantee a small reusable response
statement: All positive-generator products on finite Omega generate exactly the functions constant on common generator-signature cells, so exact future evidence expectations require their masses (and target-weighted masses). One generator with N distinct values can determine all masses via repeated posterior ratios/Vandermonde; an approximate d-bit family gives summary bits>=d+log2(1-delta) for simultaneous success1-delta. Arbitrary additive approximation can be amplified by rare evidence; the all-evidence density-ratio certificate is tanh(osc(log dQ/dP)/4). The explicit q-state chain product tree paysO(nq^3) build/O(nq^2) storage andO(q^3 log n) single local update, with a fresh forward method/ordinary incremental competitor equally equipped. Binary-chain boundary coarsening has exact uniform probability error(|a|+|b|)/(2(1+|ab|)) from acquired left/right products, even for adaptive hard endpoint evidence. New nonlocal edges or evidence outside the interface invalidate the old claim.

requires: For update-algebra claims: finite hidden space and specified positive evidence generators, with actual repeated-product closure and retained target-weighted cell masses.
For chain claims: explicit nonnegative finite-state transfer matrices, fixed interface width and the declared local/endpoint updates; all input acquisition is paid.
For approximate reuse: a fixed simultaneous response guarantee; a new dictionary/model factor or nonlocal edge needs its own earned interface.

assumptions: A few generators can distinguish every hidden state. Exact/approximate cell masses, bit storage, dense coefficient reads and chain build/update costs are real; ordinary incremental inference receives the same structures.
costs: After responses are constructed, scalar uniform error is an O(K^2) pairwise optimization; finite-target TV can use O(q log q) sign/root work per pair in exact real arithmetic, with numerical isolation/bit costs separately paid.

Exact-mass scalar coarsening sorts K values in O(K log K); retaining masses/assignments still costs O(K),a dense coefficient query costsOmega(K),and an equally informed exact scalar baseline already supports O(s) changed-coefficient updates.

Dynamic q-state chains readTheta(nq^2) entries,buildO(nq^3),storeO(nq^2),updateO(q^3 log n); a fresh O(nq^2) forward pass can be better for few/broad queries. Gaussian fixed-span reuse is ordinary Woodbury; sparse residual sketches require fixed families and known coercivity.
contract.units: Normalized target posterior error over an explicit evidence cone, evidence masses, finite-bit storage, arithmetic/bit work and model-response acquisition remain distinct.
